title: 82.8% of published entities (192,536 of 232,625) have an empty label, so labels in search, popups and graph nodes must be derived rather than read
evidence: duckdb over C3's hashed capture (e.g. osm_physical.parquet sha256 860845d7e093..., ccby3.parquet f57a8f3be46e...; hashes in docs/build/logs/next-phase/C3/SHA256SUMS): count(distinct entity_id)=232,625; filter (label is null or trim(label)='') = 192,536 (82.8%); distinct entity_type = 1 ('deployment'). Per compartment (empty/total): osm_physical 154,483/154,705; public_record 19,828/39,921; operator_accepted 12,881/21,682; dot511_ccbysa2 2,936/3,000; sig_graph 1,093/4,834; ccby3 861/861; peel_odl1 37/37; ogl_uk3 186/1,514; portal 170/5,685; ottawa_odl2 60/146; ogc_canada2 1/160; stalbert_odl1 0/80. Consequence (inference): a name index over the labelled 40,089 entities is only 17% of the record set, so label-based search, map popups and graph nodes cannot identify most records without a derivation rule (type + operator + place + source). Extends F-101/F-102 (bare codes, UUID nodes) and K12b's hub-label bug, which concern jurisdictions and graph nodes; this row quantifies record-level label emptiness in the bulk exports that feed search and the map.

title: The map island ships MapLibre's shared chunk twice: the Vite ?worker&url import bundles a second copy into the worker (≈143 KB gzip of the island's ≈425 KB gzip JS)
evidence: MapIsland.tsx:58 imports 'maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl-worker.mjs?worker&url'. Built sizes (fixtures dist, gzip -9 / brotli): MapIsland 1,054,335 raw / 282,041 gz / 232,144 br; worker 506,723 raw / 143,352 gz / 118,334 br. All 128 distinctive string literals (12-40 chars) in the worker file also occur in the MapIsland chunk (Python overlap check). maplibre-gl 6.9.0's own ESM split measured separately: maplibre-gl.mjs 147,906 gz + maplibre-gl-shared.mjs 146,250 gz + maplibre-gl-worker.mjs 6,071 gz = 300,227 gz, versus 425,393 gz today. Inference: loading the ESM split (shared chunk fetched once, module worker) would cut ≈125 KB gzip (≈29%) from the map; not verified by a rebuild. p32.15-island-budgets.md records the map at 496,905 B gzip script against a 600,000 ceiling.

title: All three public islands are client:only and hydrate into boxes that are empty before JS runs, above their no-JS fallbacks: the root cause of the /network/ and /search/ layout shift (F-115) and the empty no-JS box (F-170)
evidence: network.astro:99, search.astro:140 and map.astro:133 mount their islands with client:only="react", which renders nothing on the server; both pages say so in their own copy (map.astro:127 'with JavaScript disabled this block is empty'; network.astro:95) The .sig-island container (islands.css:13-18) reserves no height (only the map canvas, rendered by the island itself, has height:24rem at :27-31), and each island section sits above its static fallback, so hydration pushes the fallback down. C2 §6.2 Lighthouse (live): /network/ CLS 0.311 desktop, /search/ CLS 0.326 desktop, /map/ CLS 0.105; C4 §3.6: desktop /network/ CLS 0.177 on fixtures and the no-JS 'Quick filter' box renders empty. Inference: server-rendering the initial state (or mounting into a reserved box that already holds the static rendition, with client:visible/idle) removes both symptoms. Merge candidate with F-115/F-170 as their root cause.

title: The zero-JS and axe sweeps iterate a hand-maintained route list, so /releases/, /research-dossier/ and its slugs, and every export-mode-only route are never checked for scripts or WCAG: the contract fails open for new pages
evidence: ALL_PAGES = [...SHELL_PAGES, TASK_PAGE] (pages.ts:55); ZERO_JS_PUBLIC_PAGES = ALL_PAGES + JURISDICTION_DOSSIER_PAGES + FRESHNESS_SORT_PAGES + DOSSIER_PRINT minus islands (pages.ts:125-130); islands.spec.ts:13-19 asserts not.toContain('<script') only over that list; a11y.spec.ts:14 iterates A11Y_PAGES built from the same lists. SHELL_PAGES has no /releases/ and no /research-dossier/ entry although both routes are built (src/pages/releases/index.astro, src/pages/research-dossier/{index,[slug]}.astro); research-dossier.nojs.spec.ts checks content but never scripts or axe. Export-mode routes (the 55 national dossiers, their print pages) are never built in CI. Distinct from F-171 (Lighthouse matrix coverage): this is the e2e script and axe sweeps. Inference: any page added without editing pages.ts ships unchecked; C4 confirmed 0 scripts on these pages by hand only. Fix: discover routes from dist and fail on unclassified routes (K0 §4.12).
